import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy import stats

CODES = {"A": "000300.SH", "B": "000852.SH", "C": "000905.SH"}
GRID = pd.period_range("2018-12", "2025-12", freq="M")   # 85 natural months
ANA_START = pd.Period("2019-01", freq="M")
BREAK = pd.Period("2023-01", freq="M")
WINDOW = 12

# ---------- 1) month-end levels on a complete natural-month grid ----------
levels, price_rows = {}, {}
for k, code in CODES.items():
    df = data.series("index", code, start="20181201", end="20251231",
                     measure="market.cny_close", frequency="monthly", transform="level")
    if df is None or len(df) == 0:
        raise ValueError("no monthly level returned for " + code)
    mi = pd.PeriodIndex(pd.to_datetime(df["date"]), freq="M")
    s = pd.Series(np.asarray(df["value"], dtype=float), index=mi).sort_index()
    s = s[~s.index.duplicated(keep="last")]
    levels[k] = s.reindex(GRID)               # keep missing months as NaN
    price_rows[k] = int(levels[k].notna().sum())

# ---------- 2) monthly returns, no forward fill / no gap bridging ----------
rets = {}
for k in CODES:
    p = levels[k]
    r = p / p.shift(1) - 1.0                  # shift on the full grid => only adjacent months qualify
    rets[k] = r[r.index >= ANA_START]

asset_rows, audit_assets = [], []
for k in CODES:
    r = rets[k].dropna()
    vol = float(np.std(r.to_numpy(), ddof=1) * np.sqrt(12)) if len(r) >= 2 else None
    q = [float(r.quantile(x, interpolation="linear")) for x in (0.25, 0.50, 0.75)] if len(r) >= 1 else [None]*3
    miss = int(GRID.size - price_rows[k])
    asset_rows.append([CODES[k], price_rows[k], miss, int(len(r)), vol, q[0], q[1], q[2]])
    audit_assets.append({"asset": CODES[k], "price_rows": price_rows[k], "missing_months": miss,
                         "valid_returns": int(len(r)), "annual_vol": vol, "q25": q[0], "q50": q[1], "q75": q[2]})

print("=== Per-asset sample (monthly, 2019-01..2025-12) ===")
print(f"{'asset':<10}{'price_rows':>11}{'missing':>9}{'ret_n':>7}{'ann_vol':>10}{'q25':>10}{'q50':>10}{'q75':>10}")
for a in asset_rows:
    fmt = lambda v: "NA" if v is None else f"{v:.6f}"
    print(f"{a[0]:<10}{a[1]:>11}{a[2]:>9}{a[3]:>7}{fmt(a[4]):>10}{fmt(a[5]):>10}{fmt(a[6]):>10}{fmt(a[7]):>10}")

# ---------- 3) paired complete-sample statistics ----------
def ols_alpha_beta(x, y):
    res = sm.OLS(np.asarray(y, dtype=float), sm.add_constant(np.asarray(x, dtype=float))).fit()
    return float(res.params[0]), float(res.params[1])

def pair_frame(other):
    return pd.DataFrame({"a": rets["A"], "b": rets[other]}).dropna()

def pair_block(other, tag, period_label):
    df = pair_frame(other)
    if tag == "pre2023":
        df = df[df.index <= pd.Period("2022-12", freq="M")]
    elif tag == "post2023":
        df = df[df.index >= BREAK]
    n = int(len(df))
    rec = {"pair": CODES["A"] + "/" + CODES[other], "period": period_label, "n": n,
           "pearson": None, "spearman": None, "alpha_monthly": None, "beta": None}
    if n >= 3:
        rec["pearson"] = float(stats.pearsonr(df["a"].to_numpy(), df["b"].to_numpy())[0])
        rec["spearman"] = float(stats.spearmanr(df["a"].to_numpy(), df["b"].to_numpy())[0])
        rec["alpha_monthly"], rec["beta"] = ols_alpha_beta(df["a"], df["b"])
    return rec, df

pair_rows, audit_pairs = [], []
for other in ("B", "C"):
    for tag, label in (("all", "all"), ("pre2023", "pre2023"), ("post2023", "post2023")):
        rec, _ = pair_block(other, tag, label)
        audit_pairs.append(rec)
        pair_rows.append(rec)

print("\n=== Paired complete-sample statistics (y = B or C, x = A; OLS with intercept) ===")
print(f"{'pair':<22}{'period':>9}{'n':>5}{'pearson':>11}{'spearman':>11}{'alpha_m':>12}{'beta':>10}")
for r in pair_rows:
    g = lambda v: "NA" if v is None else f"{v:.6f}"
    print(f"{r['pair']:<22}{r['period']:>9}{r['n']:>5}{g(r['pearson']):>11}{g(r['spearman']):>11}{g(r['alpha_monthly']):>12}{g(r['beta']):>10}")

# ---------- 4) rolling 12 consecutive months, 12 complete paired observations ----------
def rolling_corr(other):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": rets["A"], "b": rets[other]}).dropna(how="any")
    full = pd.DataFrame({"a": rets["A"], "b": rets[other]})
    out = pd.Series(np.nan, index=full.index, dtype=float)
    idx = list(full.index)
    for i in range(WINDOW - 1, len(idx)):
        w = full.iloc[i - WINDOW + 1: i + 1]
        if w.notna().all().all():
            out.iloc[i] = float(np.corrcoef(w["a"].to_numpy(), w["b"].to_numpy())[0, 1])
    return out

roll = {o: rolling_corr(o) for o in ("B", "C")}
for o in ("B", "C"):
    v = roll[o].dropna()
    print(f"\nrolling corr A-{o}: valid_points={len(v)} "
          f"(first={str(v.index[0]) if len(v) else 'none'}, last={str(v.index[-1]) if len(v) else 'none'}, "
          f"min={float(v.min()) if len(v) else float('nan'):.6f}, max={float(v.max()) if len(v) else float('nan'):.6f})")
print("gap months inside the rolling grid (A-B): " +
      ", ".join(str(p) for p in pd.DataFrame({'a': rets['A'], 'b': rets['B']}).index[
          pd.DataFrame({'a': rets['A'], 'b': rets['B']}).isna().any(axis=1)]))
print("gap months inside the rolling grid (A-C): " +
      ", ".join(str(p) for p in pd.DataFrame({'a': rets['A'], 'b': rets['C']}).index[
          pd.DataFrame({'a': rets['A'], 'b': rets['C']}).isna().any(axis=1)]))

# ---------- 5) figures (English in-figure labels) ----------
def show(fig):
    try:
        display(fig)
    except NameError:
        print("[figure built; display() unavailable in this runtime]")
    finally:
        plt.close(fig)

xs = [p.to_timestamp(how="end") for p in GRID]
fig1, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.4))
base_note = []
for k in CODES:
    s = levels[k]
    first = s.first_valid_index()
    base_note.append(f"{k}={CODES[k]} base {first}")
    ax1.plot(xs, (s / s.loc[first] * 100.0).to_numpy(dtype=float), lw=1.7, label=f"{k} ({CODES[k]})")
ax1.axhline(100.0, color="0.6", lw=0.8, ls=":")
ax1.set_title("Month-end price levels rebased to 100 (synthetic demo, CNY)\nrebased at each series' first available grid month; gaps not filled")
ax1.set_xlabel("month end"); ax1.set_ylabel("rebased level (first available month = 100)")
ax1.legend(loc="best"); ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)
fig1.tight_layout()
show(fig1)

fig2, ax2 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.4))
for o, style in (("B", "-"), ("C", "--")):
    v = roll[o].reindex(GRID)
    dx = [p.to_timestamp(how="end") for p in v.index]
    ax2.plot(dx, v.to_numpy(dtype=float), style, lw=1.7, label=f"A vs {o} ({CODES[o]})")
ax2.axhline(0.0, color="0.6", lw=0.8, ls=":")
ax2.axvline(pd.Period("2023-01", freq="M").to_timestamp(how="end"), color="0.4", lw=0.9, ls="--")
ax2.set_ylim(-1.05, 1.05)
ax2.set_title("Rolling correlation, 12 consecutive calendar months with 12 complete paired observations\nline breaks at missing months and incomplete windows (not interpolation)")
ax2.set_xlabel("window end (month)"); ax2.set_ylabel("Pearson correlation")
ax2.legend(loc="best"); ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)
fig2.tight_layout()
show(fig2)

print("\nrebasing bases: " + " | ".join(base_note))

audit = {"assets": audit_assets, "pairs": audit_pairs}
print("AUDIT_JSON=" + json.dumps(audit, ensure_ascii=False))

Source: data.series(asset_type="index", measure="market.cny_close", frequency="monthly", transform="level", start=20181201, end=20251231). Full natural-month grid 2018-12..2025-12 (85 months); 2018-12 is warm-up only, analysis window 2019-01..2025-12 (84 months). No forward fill, no zero fill; a gap-spanning change is never treated as a one-month return (shift(1) is taken on the full grid). Returns are simple monthly, unitless decimal; annualised vol = sample std (ddof=1) x sqrt(12). Quantiles use linear interpolation. Pairs use only months where both legs and both legs' prior grid month are present. Rolling windows require 12 consecutive calendar months and 12 complete paired observations; otherwise the line breaks. Special break at 2023-01 (pre2023 = returns with month <= 2022-12; post2023 = month >= 2023-01). Limitations: synthetic series, tiny samples (n in the tens), overlapping rolling windows are not iid, no dividends/total return, no costs, correlation is not evidence of a tradable hedge.

import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy import stats

CODES = {"A": "000300.SH", "B": "000852.SH", "C": "000905.SH"}
GRID = pd.period_range("2018-12", "2025-12", freq="M")      # 85 natural months
ANA_START = pd.Period("2019-01", freq="M")
BREAK = pd.Period("2023-01", freq="M")
WINDOW = 12
XS = [p.to_timestamp(how="end") for p in GRID]

# ---------- 1) month-end levels on the complete natural-month grid ----------
levels, price_rows = {}, {}
for k, code in CODES.items():
    df = data.series("index", code, start="20181201", end="20251231",
                     measure="market.cny_close", frequency="monthly", transform="level")
    if df is None or len(df) == 0:
        raise ValueError("no monthly level returned for " + code)
    mi = pd.PeriodIndex(pd.to_datetime(df["date"]), freq="M")
    s = pd.Series(np.asarray(df["value"], dtype=float), index=mi).sort_index()
    s = s[~s.index.duplicated(keep="last")]
    levels[k] = s.reindex(GRID)                 # missing months stay NaN
    price_rows[k] = int(levels[k].notna().sum())

# ---------- 2) monthly returns (no fill, no gap bridging) ----------
rets = {}
for k in CODES:
    r = levels[k] / levels[k].shift(1) - 1.0     # prior row = prior calendar month by construction
    rets[k] = r[r.index >= ANA_START]

asset_rows, audit_assets = [], []
for k in CODES:
    r = rets[k].dropna()
    vol = float(np.std(r.to_numpy(), ddof=1) * np.sqrt(12)) if len(r) >= 2 else None
    q = [float(r.quantile(x, interpolation="linear")) for x in (0.25, 0.50, 0.75)] if len(r) else [None] * 3
    miss = int(GRID.size - price_rows[k])
    asset_rows.append([CODES[k], price_rows[k], miss, int(len(r)), vol, q[0], q[1], q[2]])
    audit_assets.append({"asset": CODES[k], "price_rows": price_rows[k], "missing_months": miss,
                         "valid_returns": int(len(r)), "annual_vol": vol, "q25": q[0], "q50": q[1], "q75": q[2]})

print("=== Per-asset sample (monthly returns, 2019-01..2025-12) ===")
print(f"{'asset':<11}{'price_rows':>11}{'missing_m':>10}{'ret_n':>7}{'ann_vol':>11}{'q25':>11}{'q50':>11}{'q75':>11}")
f6 = lambda v: "NA" if v is None else f"{v:.6f}"
for a in asset_rows:
    print(f"{a[0]:<11}{a[1]:>11}{a[2]:>10}{a[3]:>7}{f6(a[4]):>11}{f6(a[5]):>11}{f6(a[6]):>11}{f6(a[7]):>11}")

# ---------- 3) paired complete-sample statistics ----------
def pair_frame(other):
    return pd.DataFrame({"a": rets["A"], "b": rets[other]}).dropna()

def pair_block(other, tag, label):
    df = pair_frame(other)
    if tag == "pre2023":
        df = df[df.index <= pd.Period("2022-12", freq="M")]
    elif tag == "post2023":
        df = df[df.index >= BREAK]
    n = int(len(df))
    rec = {"pair": CODES["A"] + "/" + CODES[other], "period": label, "n": n,
           "pearson": None, "spearman": None, "alpha_monthly": None, "beta": None}
    if n >= 3:
        rec["pearson"] = float(stats.pearsonr(df["a"].to_numpy(), df["b"].to_numpy())[0])
        rec["spearman"] = float(stats.spearmanr(df["a"].to_numpy(), df["b"].to_numpy())[0])
        fit = sm.OLS(df["b"].to_numpy(dtype=float),
                     sm.add_constant(df["a"].to_numpy(dtype=float))).fit()
        rec["alpha_monthly"] = float(fit.params[0])
        rec["beta"] = float(fit.params[1])
    return rec, df

pair_rows, audit_pairs = [], []
for other in ("B", "C"):
    for tag in ("all", "pre2023", "post2023"):
        rec, _ = pair_block(other, tag, tag)
        audit_pairs.append(rec)
        pair_rows.append(rec)

print("\n=== Paired complete samples (y = B or C, x = A; OLS with intercept) ===")
print(f"{'pair':<22}{'period':>9}{'n':>5}{'pearson':>11}{'spearman':>11}{'alpha_m':>13}{'beta':>11}")
for r in pair_rows:
    print(f"{r['pair']:<22}{r['period']:>9}{r['n']:>5}{f6(r['pearson']):>11}"
          f"{f6(r['spearman']):>11}{f6(r['alpha_monthly']):>13}{f6(r['beta']):>11}")

# ---------- 4) rolling 12 consecutive months with 12 complete paired observations ----------
def rolling_corr(other):
    full = pd.DataFrame({"a": rets["A"], "b": rets[other]})
    out = pd.Series(np.nan, index=full.index, dtype=float)
    for i in range(WINDOW - 1, len(full)):
        w = full.iloc[i - WINDOW + 1: i + 1]
        if w.notna().all().all():
            out.iloc[i] = float(np.corrcoef(w["a"].to_numpy(), w["b"].to_numpy())[0, 1])
    return out

roll = {o: rolling_corr(o) for o in ("B", "C")}
for o in ("B", "C"):
    v = roll[o].dropna()
    ms = pd.DataFrame({"a": rets["A"], "b": rets[o]})
    miss_m = [str(p) for p in ms.index[ms.isna().any(axis=1)]]
    print(f"\nA-{o}: gaps in paired grid -> {', '.join(miss_m) if miss_m else 'none'}")
    print(f"A-{o}: valid 12m windows = {len(v)} "
          f"({str(v.index[0]) if len(v) else 'none'} .. {str(v.index[-1]) if len(v) else 'none'}); "
          f"min={float(v.min()) if len(v) else float('nan'):.6f}; "
          f"max={float(v.max()) if len(v) else float('nan'):.6f}")

# ---------- 5) charts: contiguous segments, no interpolation across gaps ----------
def runs_of(s):
    out, cur = [], None
    for p, v in s.items():
        if pd.notna(v):
            if cur is None:
                cur = []
                out.append(cur)
            cur.append((p, float(v)))
        else:
            cur = None
    return out

def segment_frame(series_map, names):
    frame = pd.DataFrame({"date": XS})
    labels, report = {}, []
    for stem, s in series_map.items():
        rs = runs_of(s.reindex(GRID))
        if len(rs) <= 1:
            col = stem
            frame[col] = s.reindex(GRID).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            labels[col] = names[stem]
            report.append(f"{names[stem]}: " +
                          (f"{rs[0][0][0]}..{rs[0][-1][0]} (1 segment)" if rs else "no data"))
            continue
        for i, run in enumerate(rs, start=1):
            col = f"{stem}_s{i}"
            arr = np.full(GRID.size, np.nan)
            for p, v in run:
                arr[GRID.get_loc(p)] = v
            frame[col] = arr
            labels[col] = f"{names[stem]} [{i}]"
        report.append(f"{names[stem]}: {len(rs)} segments -> " +
                      "; ".join(f"{r[0][0]}..{r[-1][0]}" for r in rs))
    return frame, labels, report

norm = {}
for k in CODES:
    s = levels[k]
    norm[k] = s / s.loc[s.first_valid_index()] * 100.0

px_frame, px_labels, px_report = segment_frame(norm, {k: f"{k} ({CODES[k]})" for k in CODES})
charts.line(px_frame, x="date", y=list(px_labels.keys()),
            title="Month-end levels rebased to 100 (synthetic demo, CNY); breaks = missing months",
            labels=px_labels)

cr_frame, cr_labels, cr_report = segment_frame(
    roll, {"B": f"A vs B ({CODES['B']})", "C": f"A vs C ({CODES['C']})"})
charts.line(cr_frame, x="date", y=list(cr_labels.keys()),
            title="Rolling correlation, 12 consecutive months / 12 complete pairs; breaks = missing or short window",
            labels=cr_labels)

print("\nrebasing bases (first available grid month = 100): " +
      " | ".join(f"{k}={CODES[k]}@{levels[k].first_valid_index()}" for k in CODES))
print("price-curve segments: " + " || ".join(px_report))
print("rolling-corr segments: " + " || ".join(cr_report))

print("AUDIT_JSON=" + json.dumps({"assets": audit_assets, "pairs": audit_pairs}, ensure_ascii=False))
inputScope: Authorized SYNTHETIC demo, not real market data. Three isolated month-end price series in CNY: A=000300.SH, B=000852.SH, C=000905.SH (local library holds 85/82/81 month-end rows). Source: data.series(asset_type="index", measure="market.cny_close", frequency="monthly", transform="level", start=20181201, end=20251231). Full natural-month grid 2018-12..2025-12 (85 months); 2018-12 is warm-up only, analysis window 2019-01..2025-12 (84 months). No forward fill, no zero fill; returns are p_t/p_(prior grid month)-1 with the shift taken on the full grid, so a change spanning a missing month is never recorded as a one-month return. Returns are unitless decimals; annualised vol = sample std (ddof=1) x sqrt(12); quantiles interpolated linearly. Pairs use months where both legs and both prior grid months exist. Rolling windows demand 12 consecutive calendar months AND 12 complete paired observations; lines are drawn as separate contiguous segments so missing months and short windows are visible breaks. Special split at 2023-01 (pre2023: month<=2022-12; post2023: month>=2023-01). Limitations: synthetic; n in the tens; overlapping rolling windows are not iid; price indices exclude dividends; no costs; correlation is not proof of a tradable hedge; isolated library, do not compare with the real indices.
